$comment: document: a case study's fields as contract/collections/case-studies.json defines them, as the case-study view receives them. Stored as defined: title, client, summary, results, details, challenge and solution (rich text HTML, a stored h3 renders h3 at base 2), gallery (media ids), externalUrl. Resolved for the view: image is featuredImage (a media id); client and sector are the names the view draws (the record's title when the site enables the record's collection and it resolves, otherwise the free text, SC-035); services are resolved to { id, title, href }, href null for a service with no public page. The view takes labels back, results, challenge, solution, gallery, liveSite and services from site.labels, and the back link's address from site.collectionIndexes['case-study'] (the case studies' index). site.caseStudy is left out, so the header is plain, the default (case-study/band draws it as a band). Two images, each its own field (SC-034): image is featuredImage, the hero image, drawn last in the header and the only priority image; caseStudyImage is drawn in the flow between the challenge and the solution, lazy, and not at all when it names the featured image's media item (media identity is the media id, never the alt text or the file name).
summary: A case study with every part set: in the story, a link back to the index, the title, the summary, the featured image as the hero and priority image, a challenge, the case-study image, a solution whose stored h3 renders h3, three results, a gallery of two images and the live-site link opening in a new tab; in the aside, three project details, the client, the sector and two delivered services, each linked to its page.

document.challenge: The walls were sound, but forty years of bramble and ash saplings had taken the beds, and the glasshouse had lost most of its glass.
document.solution:
We cleared the garden by hand to keep the old box edging, then laid out the beds again on the original plan.

Planting for the café

The planting follows the café's menu through the year, with salad and herbs nearest the kitchen door.
